Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

poor adjective

to be pitied

also poor thing, poor you, miserable, wretched

classical

Catull. 8.1: miser Catulle
Traupman 156, 363, 155

miser, misera, miserum

adjective, declension

poor, unhappy, to be pitied

In exclamations, the accusative: Mē miserum!, poor me!; Miseram Mārcellam!, poor Marcella! (Traupman 23).

Other words

  • misellus, misella, misellum — poor little …

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Catull. 3.16; Cic. Att. 3.23.6 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Catull.; Cic. in epistulīs)

Examples

  • ō factum male! ō miselle passer!

    oh, what a shame! poor little sparrow!Catull. 3.16

  • pōma sumus Cybelēs: procul hinc discēde, viātor, nē cadat in miserum nostra ruīna caput

    we are Cybele’s fruit: keep away, traveller, or we’ll fall on your poor headMart. 13.25.1–2

See also poor, oh dear!.

SourcesLewis & Short: miser · Lewis & Short: misellus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 23, 156, 363.
